item.text:
As of **August 28, 2026**, the newest **published** MCP specification revision I found is **`2026-07-28`**. The official GitHub releases page describes `2026-07-28` as the **stable release** of that revision, the draft spec page says the draft points to the **latest version (`2026-07-28`)**, and the older `2025-11-25` spec page also says **“View the latest version (2026-07-28)”**.  
Sources: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/releases, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25

The **preceding revision** is **`2025-11-25`**; the `2026-07-28` changelog explicitly says it lists changes since **`2025-11-25`**.  
Source: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog

**Supported fact: biggest changes in `2026-07-28`** include removal of the `initialize` / `notifications/initialized` handshake; a new stateless core with required per-request `_meta`; required `server/discover`; MRTR replacing prior server-initiated requests; required `resultType` on results; replacement of some notification/subscription behavior with `subscriptions/listen`; removal of `ping`, `logging/setLevel`, and `notifications/roots/list_changed`; required cache metadata (`ttlMs`, `cacheScope`) on list/read results; deterministic `tools/list` ordering guidance; looser JSON Schema support; and deprecation of Roots, Sampling, and Logging.  
Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/deprecated

**Inference: for local tool servers, the changes that matter most are these, in roughly this order.**

1. **Statelessness and removal of `initialize` matter most.**  
   Why: `2026-07-28` says MCP is now stateless; servers **MUST NOT** rely on prior requests on the same connection; clients **SHOULD NOT** use a task/thread/conversation as the lifetime boundary for a **stdio** process; and cross-request state must be carried by explicit identifiers. For local servers, stdio is the standard “client launches the server as a subprocess” transport, so this directly changes how a local server must model context and process lifetime.  
   Sources for the facts: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle

2. **`server/discover` is the next most important change.**  
   Why: servers **MUST** implement it in `2026-07-28`, and the spec says it is the recommended backward-compatibility probe on **stdio**. That is directly relevant to local servers that need to coexist with both legacy (`initialize`-based) and modern clients.  
   Sources for the facts: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog

3. **MRTR plus mandatory `resultType` is a major behavioral change for interactive local tools.**  
   Why: `2026-07-28` replaces prior server-initiated requests such as `roots/list`, `sampling/createMessage`, and `elicitation/create` with `InputRequiredResult` plus retry via `inputResponses`, and all results now require `resultType`. Any local server that relied on the old bidirectional request pattern has to rework its control flow.  
   Sources for the facts: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic

4. **Deprecation/removal around Roots, Sampling, and Logging matters if the server used those features.**  
   Why: `2026-07-28` deprecates Roots, Sampling, and Logging; removes `logging/setLevel`; moves log level to per-request `_meta`; and says stdio servers should log to `stderr`. That is especially relevant to local subprocess servers because stdio logging behavior is explicitly called out.  
   Sources for the facts: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/deprecated, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio

5. **Tool-catalog caching changes matter for local servers with nontrivial `tools/list` output.**  
   Why: `2026-07-28` says `tools/list` results should be deterministic and now require `ttlMs` and `cacheScope`. That affects how local servers expose changing tool inventories and how clients cache them.  
   Sources for the facts: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover

6. **Schema loosening matters, but usually after the transport/lifecycle changes above.**  
   Why: `2026-07-28` allows any JSON Schema 2020-12 keywords in `inputSchema`/`outputSchema`, supports explicit dialects, and requires support for 2020-12 by default. That can affect local tool servers with richer schemas, but it is usually less disruptive than the protocol-flow changes.  
   Sources for the facts: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools

**Supported fact: changes that matter less to local stdio tool servers** are mostly the HTTP-specific ones: header-based routing, `Mcp-Session-Id` removal, GET endpoint removal, SSE resumability removal, and most authorization changes. The stdio transport has **no header layer**, and the authorization spec says stdio implementations **SHOULD NOT** follow the HTTP authorization spec and should instead retrieve credentials from the environment.  
Sources: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog

**Uncertainty:** “matter most” is not ranked by the spec itself; that prioritization is my inference from the normative changes above and from the fact that local servers commonly use the stdio subprocess transport.  
Sources for the underlying facts: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog

**Disagreement:** I found no conflicting official MCP source, among the pages above, about the latest published revision being `2026-07-28`.  

**Lack of good evidence:** I did not find an official source that explicitly defines “local tool servers” as a formal spec category; treating that phrase as primarily **stdio client-launched subprocess servers** is an inference from the transport docs.  
Sources for the underlying facts: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports
